## Review

_Congratulations, you've completed this exercise and learned a lot about stacked pull requests._

<img src="https://octodex.github.com/images/jetpacktocat.png" alt="celebrate" width=200 align=right>

Here's a recap of your accomplishments:

- You learned how a stack chains pull requests, with each one targeting the branch below it.
- You built layered branches, each created from the one below it, on the GitHub website.
- You opened pull requests with chained base branches and linked them as a stack.
- You merged a stack from the bottom up and saw the remaining pull requests re-target `main`.

### What's next?

- Learn how to keep a stack in sync in [Managing stacked pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/create-pull-requests/managing-stacked-pull-requests).
- Prefer the terminal? Try the [Quickstart for stacked pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/get-started/stacked-prs-quickstart) with the `gh stack` extension, and let Copilot help with `gh skill install github/gh-stack` and [Stack AI-generated code in pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/tutorials/stack-ai-generated-code-in-pull-requests).
- Bring stacks to your team with [Roll out stacked pull requests to your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/tutorials/roll-out-stacked-prs).
